invertPointPostcondition.contract: fk_surface_algo.h31–38: true yields UV on surface within tolerance, near input estimate by periodic unwrapping.
invertPointPostcondition.finding: Newton/projection residual checked before final unwrapNear; unwrapping adds rounded IEEE multiples of approximate period, changing the evaluated point. Returning true unconditionally after unwrap fails the delivered-UV postcondition.

rootReportedWitness.attribution: Executed by parent/root, not this observer; numerical values are root-reported.

invertPointPostcondition.proposal: After every UV mutation and final unwrap: if UV nonfinite return false before surface evaluation; evaluate final distance and return finite(distance)&&distance<=tolerance. Keep chosen periodic branch, no canonical reset/slack.
invertPointPostcondition.semanticLimit: Conservative false may indicate no sufficiently accurate double UV near the requested branch, not proof that p lies off the mathematical surface.
invertPointPostcondition.candidateAudit: No static blocker: finite UV short-circuits invalid evaluation; final physical residual must be finite and <= unchanged tolerance, after BSpline branch decisions and periodic unwrap. No change to Newton iterations/projection/branch choice.
remainingLimits: Only invertPoint output at return is checked. Later caller-side UV mutations, manual periodic unwrapping or nearPole regularization are outside this guard.
Callers must respect false; this review does not establish behavior of code which ignores the return value.
A point on the mathematical surface can conservatively yield false if a nearby unwrapped double parameter cannot deliver the requested physical accuracy. No global impossibility claim.
This is a final evaluated residual check, not an interval certificate of projection global optimality or Newton convergence.
